triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

An extremely common standalone complaint, though currently 'poor sleep' mostly surfaces only as a feature of other diagnoses. Insomnia with excessive daytime sleepiness and witnessed apnoeas should prompt consideration of obstructive sleep apnoea instead.
workup: Screen for depression, anxiety, caffeine/alcohol use, and other primary sleep disorders
CBT for insomnia (CBT-I) is first-line and more durable than medication

conditions.name: Menopause

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: The natural transition marking the end of menstrual periods, typically age 45-55 -- hot flushes and night sweats (no dedicated evidence node exists for these directly; heat intolerance is used here as an imperfect proxy, a disclosed limitation) disrupting sleep, along with mood changes, 'brain fog', and joint aches, developing gradually over months as periods become irregular and then stop. A normal life transition, not a disease -- but genuinely disruptive symptoms are common and treatable, and shouldn't be dismissed. Bleeding after 12 months without a period (postmenopausal bleeding) is NOT a normal menopause symptom and needs assessment to exclude a gynaecological cause.
workup: Usually a clinical diagnosis based on age and symptom pattern -- hormone testing is not usually needed to diagnose menopause itself in a woman with typical symptoms at a typical age
Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) -- the most effective treatment for hot flushes/night sweats and genitourinary symptoms, for appropriately selected women without contraindications
Non-hormonal options (certain antidepressants, lifestyle measures) where HRT isn't suitable or preferred
Any bleeding after 12 months without a period needs assessment -- this is NOT a normal menopause symptom

conditions.name: Goitre (simple/iodine-deficiency)

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: A visible or palpable enlargement of the thyroid gland, most commonly from dietary iodine deficiency -- a genuinely significant public health issue in parts of India, particularly the Himalayan belt and other iodine-deficient regions. Unlike Hypothyroidism/Hyperthyroidism sharing this bundle, simple goitre is usually EUTHYROID (normal thyroid function) -- no weight change, temperature intolerance or mood change, since the gland is simply enlarged, not over- or under-active. No dedicated 'visible neck swelling' evidence node exists anywhere in this checker -- the actual presenting complaint -- so this is assessed on examination rather than a specific symptom question.
workup: Thyroid function tests (TSH, T4) -- to confirm the gland is functioning normally, distinguishing simple goitre from Hypothyroidism/Hyperthyroidism
Urinary iodine estimation where iodine deficiency is suspected
Iodised salt and correcting dietary iodine intake -- the standard public-health and individual measure
Ultrasound and/or referral if the gland is rapidly enlarging, hard, or asymmetric, to exclude a nodule needing separate assessment

exam.step: Ask specifically about the urge-to-move sensation and its relationship to rest/evening and movement
exam.positive: The genuine diagnostic hallmark -- not captured by a dedicated node in this checker, an important disclosed limitation

exam.step: Ask about memory, gait, tremor and rigidity, looking for their ABSENCE
exam.positive: RLS does not cause these -- their presence should prompt considering a Parkinson's/dementia-spectrum condition instead, sharing this bundle

labs.test: Clinical history against standard diagnostic criteria
labs.confirms: The actual basis for diagnosis -- there is no single confirmatory test
Identifies a genuine, treatable contributing factor

conditions.name: Restless legs syndrome

triage.label: Routine
triage.action: Discuss with your doctor at a routine appointment

conditions.summary: An uncomfortable urge to move the legs, typically worse in the evening/at rest and relieved by movement, genuinely disrupting sleep. DISCLOSED PROXY: no evidence node in this catalogue captures this actual diagnostic hallmark directly -- modelled here through its genuine downstream effect (sleep disturbance) and the real nocturnal worsening pattern. Distinct from the dementia/Parkinson's-cluster conditions sharing this bundle: RLS does not cause memory loss, confusion, tremor or rigidity.
workup: Ask specifically about an urge to move the legs with an uncomfortable sensation, worse in the evening/at rest, relieved by movement -- the genuine diagnostic criteria, not directly captured by a node here
Check ferritin -- iron deficiency is a genuine, common, treatable contributor to RLS, even without frank anaemia
Review medication list (certain antidepressants, antihistamines can worsen RLS)
Iron replacement if ferritin is low; dopamine agonists or other medication for persistent, significant symptoms, under specialist guidance

redFlags.label: Possible sepsis
redFlags.message: A fever together with confusion, very fast breathing, mottled skin or a collapsing blood pressure can mean infection is affecting the whole body.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now. Do not wait to see whether it settles.

redFlags.label: Rash that does not fade under pressure
redFlags.message: Spots that stay visible when a glass is pressed on them, alongside feeling unwell, can be a sign of bacteria in the bloodstream.

redFlags.label: Possible severe allergic reaction
redFlags.message: Swelling of the throat or tongue with difficulty breathing after a food, sting, or medicine can close the airway within minutes.
redFlags.action: Use an adrenaline auto-injector if you have one, then call emergency services.

redFlags.label: Reduced consciousness
redFlags.message: Being difficult to rouse, or drifting in and out of awareness, always needs immediate assessment whatever the cause.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now. Place the person on their side if unresponsive.

redFlags.label: Possible stroke
redFlags.message: Sudden facial drooping, arm weakness or difficulty speaking is a stroke until proven otherwise. Treatment works only within a few hours.
redFlags.action: Call emergency services now and note the exact time symptoms began.

redFlags.label: Seizure
redFlags.message: A first seizure needs assessment to find the cause and to advise on driving and safety.
redFlags.action: Seek urgent assessment today. Call emergency services if the seizure lasted over five minutes or a second one followed.

redFlags.label: Significant gastrointestinal bleeding
redFlags.message: Vomiting blood, or passing black tarry stools, means bleeding inside the digestive tract.
redFlags.action: Go to an emergency department now.

redFlags.label: New jaundice
redFlags.message: Yellowing of the skin or eyes always needs blood tests to find out why.

redFlags.label: Sudden loss of vision
redFlags.message: Sight lost suddenly in one or both eyes needs assessment the same hour, whatever the cause.
redFlags.action: Go to an eye emergency department now.

redFlags.label: Thoughts of self-harm
redFlags.message: Thoughts of harming yourself or of being better off dead deserve help today. You do not have to be in crisis to reach out.
redFlags.action: Contact your doctor, a crisis line, or go to an emergency department now. If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services.

redFlags.label: New confusion coming on over hours or days
redFlags.message: Confusion that has come on over hours or days, or that comes and goes through the day, is delirium until proven otherwise. It is caused by something else -- an infection, a drug, pain, retention -- and that cause needs finding today.
redFlags.action: Seek same-day medical assessment. Take a list of all medications. Call emergency services if they are drowsy, feverish or cannot be roused properly.

disclaimer: This tool provides information about possible causes of symptoms. It is not a diagnosis and it cannot examine you. It does not replace assessment by a qualified clinician. If you feel very unwell, or your symptoms are getting rapidly worse, seek medical help immediately regardless of what this tool says.
